newsitem.title: RUSSIA: RUSSIA'S RTS WANTS TO RELAUNCH TRADE IN GAZPROM. [CORRECTED 15:47 GMT]
newsitem.headline: RUSSIA'S RTS WANTS TO RELAUNCH TRADE IN GAZPROM. [CORRECTED 15:47 GMT]

text.p: The Russian Trading System said on Tuesday it was seeking permission to relaunch trade in shares of natural gas monopoly Gazprom, removed from RTS trade on July 3.

The Russian Trading System is an electronic over the counter trading system. The RTS index of 21 shares is published by the NAUFOR brokers association (corrects from "It also publishes a share index composed of 22 shares").
"We're waiting...we're naturally trying to get Gazprom back," said RTS president Dmitry Ponomaryov.
Ponomaryov, speaking after a news conference, also said the RTS board would vote on a proposed depositary agreement with the Depositary Clearing Company (DKK) on September 5.
He said the agreement would allow the RTS, which does not currently require deals to be registered and has no depositary or clearing system, to guarantee delivery of shares.
But a settlement system for participants, who now frequently arrange payment between themselves through off-shore currency accounts, remains a problem for the future, he said.
"For the market, of course, money is the main issue -- how to move from currency to roubles, but so far we haven't been able to resolve that," Ponomaryov said.

Although trade in shares of a few leading Russian companies has started on the Moscow Interbank Currency Exchange and some regional exchanges, the Russian Trading System handles the bulk of trade in equities.

A government decree in late May, however, transferred trade in Gazprom from the RTS and other trading systems, which were required to observe Gazprom's right of first refusal in sales of its shares, to four so-called "organised markets".
The decree exempted the four regional exchanges from the right of first refusal.

Ponomaryov said RTS was seeking to be allowed to trade in so-called "cleaned" shares, already refused by Gazprom, and ultimately wanted to be included in the list of "organised markets" allowed to trade in all Gazprom shares.

The government decree was part of efforts to bring Gazprom's lucrative natural gas empire firmly under federal jurisdiction, efforts senior government officials had said were aimed at boosting Gazprom's bobbing share price.
But Gazprom chairman Rem Vyakhirev said last week he was not impressed with the results of the changes so far.
"We will apply all our strength to organise (trade) properly, because volumes are low and prices are behaving strangely," Vyakhirev said.
"I am not satisfied with the current work of all trading points, let's put it that way."
